second_order: rallying people to draw Rocket League on the canvas
theme_note: Calls, explanations, visibility work and explicit joining all recruit people into a shared Rocket League mark.

second_order: working out what Psyonix's April Fools joke is
theme_note: Questions, evidence, corrections and announcements collectively identify which game change is the joke and how it works.

second_order: building the logo from a shared plan
theme_note: Color choices, pixel order, visible shapes, error reports and shifts of labor are all ways participants turn a proposal into a recognizable shared drawing.

second_order: carrying the canvas plan through Discord and templates
theme_note: These passages move a common design or coordination venue into the work, rather than merely naming a link.

second_order: making deals and swapping help with canvas neighbours
theme_note: Alliance, permission, reciprocal defense, accidental overwriting, peace and reminders all negotiate what adjacent groups may do and owe one another.

second_order: keeping the logo repaired and recognizable
theme_note: Near-constant maintenance and reports of the logo melting describe the repeated work of keeping a finished-looking image intact.

second_order: teasing putting white squares over the logo
theme_note: This isolated code is a joking threat to interfere with the community drawing and belongs with no other practice yet.
People turn temporary rank names into identities, achievements, teasing, puns, and ordinary game talk; what varies is whether they embrace, reject, or merely reuse a name.

second_order: asking to keep veggie ranks, flairs and rewards
theme_note: Petitions, settings, modes, flairs, titles, rewards and continuing use all try to carry the one-day joke forward; some ask instead for the normal ranks back.

second_order: making and unpacking other April Fools jokes
theme_note: Hamburger and Meat ranks, fake modes and trailers, rickrolls, inventories and lag-prank claims are separate acts of making, extending or explaining jokes beyond the vegetable-rank practice.

second_order: judging the prank against the game they wanted fixed
theme_note: Participants praise or fault the joke by comparing it with servers, Xbox faults, competitive presentation and developer effort, while others defend the timing and work.

second_order: showing, celebrating and recounting the canvas work
theme_note: Displays, timelapses, thanks, credit, pride and end-of-event recollections make the shared work visible and argue over how it was made.

second_order: challenging who planned the work and who gets credit
theme_note: Challenges to moderators, Discord organizers, alliance consent, unplanned expansion and bot claims all dispute who can say 'we' or claim the result.

second_order: asking the room to stop posting and let r/place go
theme_note: These passages ask organizers to keep it on Discord, stop the spam, or move on after battles and repeated calls.

second_order: turning Brisk sponsorship into a rank joke
theme_note: Participants propose, explain, welcome and criticize a Brisk rank while arguing about the sponsor meme and product placement.

second_order: proposing posted GT pixel art for r/place
theme_note: A displayed GT pixel art prompts a locationless proposal and agreement to put it on the canvas; no later code turns it into a plan.

second_order: arguing over calling the logo's mark a 'Gay Touch'
theme_note: The repair call's phrase sets off challenges, denial, questions and a repeated joke; the thread discusses the wording more than it organizes repair.

second_order: recreating the Rocket League logo on Place 2
theme_note: Friends remake the earlier logo on a clone, identify the venue, credit helpers and leave one reader asking what Place 2 is.
